transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, thanks for seeing me. I guess... well, I came in because I just can't seem to get out of my own head lately. I keep feeling like I’ve just completely let my family down, and it all really traces back to taking on this mortgage. We bought this place and I thought, you know, I went to college for a bit, I'm 38, I should be able to handle a house, right? But the pressure of it is just... it's eating me alive. I feel like I made this massive mistake and trapped my family in this financial hole. 

And it just spills over into everything, especially my job. I wait tables, and lately it's like every single shift is just a test that I'm failing. If I make even a small mistake—like ringing in a medium-rare steak instead of medium, or forgetting to bring extra napkins to a table when we're slammed—it doesn't just feel like a regular mistake. It feels like absolute proof that I’m useless. I just stand there in the server station thinking about the mortgage and thinking about how I can't even get a basic dinner order right, so of course I've messed up my family's life. It just makes me feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me, you know? Like I'm just dragging everyone down because I'm not capable of doing anything right, and I just can't shake that heavy feeling no matter what I do.
How long have you been feeling this way—was there a specific point when it started, and has it been present nearly every day since then?

Well, let me think back, because the timeline is... it's pretty much burned into my brain at this point. It’s been going on for about a year and eight months. Yeah, a year and eight months, because it was right after we finally closed on the condo and took on that mortgage. 

I remember the day we got the keys, I was supposed to be thrilled, right? We had been looking for a place for a while, saving up whatever tips I could, and we finally got this condo. But almost the second the ink dried on those mortgage papers, instead of feeling happy or proud, this... this massive weight just dropped right onto my chest. I thought it was just buyer's remorse at first, you know, just normal jitters. But it never went away. 

And as for whether it's every day, honestly, yes, Dr. Smith. It is every single day. I wake up, and before I even get out of bed, before I even go to the kitchen to make coffee, my very first thought is just this overwhelming dread about the money and how I've trapped my family. It doesn't take a day off. Whether it's a Tuesday morning or a Saturday night when I'm slammed at the restaurant trying to remember who ordered what, it's just always there in the background. Every day for the last twenty months, just this constant, heavy loop of feeling like a total failure because I took on this condo. I keep hoping I'll wake up and the cloud will be gone, but it just hasn't stopped.
Over these past 20 months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with people?

Yeah... yeah, I really have. It's funny you ask about spending time with people because, well, working in a restaurant, you're constantly around people, right? And I used to actually really enjoy that part of the job. We have these regulars who come in, like this older couple who always asks for my section, or the guys who come in for half-price apps on Thursdays, and I used to stand there and joke around with them for five, ten minutes at a time. I had this whole banter going. It made the shift go by faster, and I actually liked making them laugh. 

But now... I don't know, that feeling is just completely gone. I walk up to a table and I just keep my face completely straight. I don't smile, I don't make those little jokes or ask how their week was. I just ask what they want to drink, write it down, and walk away. I really only say exactly what I have to say to get the order in and get the food to the table. I just don't have the energy to put on that friendly face, and honestly, I just don't care to. 

And it's not just at work with strangers, either. It's with my own family, like my brother. We used to be pretty close, and we had this routine where I'd text him after my evening shifts, usually around 11 or 11:30 at night when I was finally off my feet and unwinding. We'd just shoot the breeze, complain about our days, maybe talk about sports, just normal brother stuff. But for a long time now, he'll text me, and I'll see the notification light up on my phone screen... and I just stare at it. I'll read what he said, but I just let the messages sit there. Sometimes for days. I just don't feel that... that pull to answer him anymore. It's not that I'm mad at him, or that we had a fight or anything like that. It's just this total blankness where the urge to talk to him used to be. It's like the part of me that used to care about connecting with people, even my own brother, just completely shut off. I know I should probably reply so he doesn't worry about me, but I just look at the phone, put it down on the counter, and walk away because I just can't bring myself to care enough to type anything back.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, that life isn't worth living, or that you'd be better off dead?

I want to be really clear about this right off the bat, Dr. Smith, because I know it's a heavy question and I don't want to alarm you. I don't have a plan to hurt myself. I'm not... I'm not sitting around trying to figure out a way to do something drastic, because honestly, I know that would just leave my family in an even worse financial hole with the condo and the mortgage, and I've already done enough damage there by taking it on in the first place. So no, no actual plans or anything like that. 

But... well, the honest truth is, the mornings are just incredibly hard for me. Especially when I have an early shift. Sometimes they schedule me to open the restaurant, which means I have to be in early to get the patio set up, wipe down all the menus, make sure the coffee stations are totally stocked before we even unlock the front doors. And I'll just be lying awake in bed for hours before my alarm is even supposed to go off, just staring up at the ceiling in the dark. The house is totally quiet, but my head is just spinning with all the mistakes I've made, the money, the fact that I'm 38 and just failing at everything I touch. 

And in those moments, just lying there before that early shift... I do sometimes think that it would just be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I could just drift off and not open my eyes again, then I wouldn't have to keep going into work and messing up basic orders, and I wouldn't have to keep feeling this crushing weight of letting everyone down every single day. It's not that I want to take my own life, it's just this really intense, heavy wish that I could just... not wake up, so the failing would finally just stop.

Are you still able to go to your shifts and get through your day-to-day responsibilities, even though it's very hard, or have you found yourself unable to work or complete basic daily tasks because of how you're feeling?

Well, I mean, I am still going. I haven't completely stopped showing up, but... honestly, it's getting really, really close to that point. It's a massive struggle just to keep my head above water. I haven't actually been fired or totally no-showed, but I’ve had these near-missed shifts lately where I'm literally running through the alley to the back door of the restaurant with like, one minute to spare, just because I couldn't get myself out of the house. 

And once I'm actually on the floor, getting through the day-to-day stuff is... it's like wading through wet cement. I've been having so much trouble keeping up with the POS reports—that's our Point of Sale computer system—and usually, closing out my tables and running my checkout at the end of the night takes me maybe five, ten minutes tops. But lately, I'm just staring at the screen at the end of a shift, and the numbers just sort of blur together. I'm making stupid mistakes on the reports. And they sometimes have me help with inventory, you know, counting the liquor bottles in the back or the dry goods in the pantry, and I'll completely lose my place and write down the wrong counts. It's terrifying, honestly, because every time I mess up a count or a report, I just think, this is it, my manager is going to write me up, and if I lose this job, then I can't pay the mortgage, and then we lose the condo. 

And the mistakes aren't just happening at the restaurant. It’s the home stuff, too. I was trying to sort out some of the mortgage paperwork the other week—just some basic stuff they needed regarding the escrow account and the property taxes—and I completely botched it. I was looking at the forms, and my brain just wouldn't process what I was reading, and I ended up making mistakes on it that I had to call the bank in a panic to fix. 

So, yeah, I'm physically there, but I'm dropping the ball everywhere. And people are definitely starting to notice that I'm not myself. Because I've pulled back so much from my brother, like I was saying, and from the other servers... it's getting obvious. One of the bartenders actually pulled me aside by the waitstation the other day and asked if I was sick or if something was wrong at home, because I guess I've just been acting like a total ghost. My brother's made comments too, asking what's going on with me. So I am doing the bare minimum to not get fired or default on the house, but it feels like I'm just one bad day away from the whole house of cards coming down.
